counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span confirming Schistosoma ova in urine or stool
No raw span excluding neurocysticercosis by serology or imaging
No raw span explicitly naming schistosomal myelitis
decisive_items: He reported a 1-month history of drinking unsafe water
Routine blood tests showed a white-cell count of 4430 cells/mm3 with 450 eosinophils

Magnetic resonance imaging of the spine demonstrated an enhancing intramedullary mass involving the conus medullaris at the L1–L2 level, findings that suggested an arteriovenous malformation or a cavernoma
response.rationale: R6 is the only candidate that integrates the raw epidemiological clue of unsafe water, the raw eosinophilia, and the conus medullaris syndrome; the enhancing conus mass is compatible with ectopic spinal schistosomiasis. R1 only reuses the nonspecific intramedullary mass, while R2 and R4 are correlated restatements of the same MRI differential and do not explain the exposure and eosinophilia.

rejected.why: Its only raw support is the nonspecific enhancing intramedullary mass; it lacks raw evidence for unsafe water exposure or eosinophilia and is a less coherent fit for acute urinary retention and conus involvement.
Its raw support is the same MRI differential as R4 and lacks the raw exposure and eosinophilia clues; discounted as a correlated restatement of the imaging differential.
Its raw support is the same MRI differential as R2 and lacks the raw exposure and eosinophilia clues; discounted as a correlated restatement of the imaging differential.
